parts.text: We need to refactor the pipeline observer interface so it does not accumulate callbacks. I also want tests and metrics.
Understood. I'll propose an observer/event approach, add a minimal API surface, and validate with unit tests and Prometheus counters.
Here are notes from production: we saw memory growth, and some requests had 90k prompt tokens. Stack traces mention history-context serialization.
Likely causes: oversized tool payloads and unbounded system injections (preferences + RAG) crowd out history. We'll add token-aware caps and compression.
Can you also ensure the last user message is never dropped, even if it's huge?
Yes. We'll implement emergency truncation (head/tail/highlights) for a single oversized anchor message.
Now imagine 40 more turns of back-and-forth discussing constraints, budgets, and edge cases. Keep the concrete details.
We'll keep anchors and the latest tool chain, compress older content deterministically, and enforce per-source budgets.
REPEAT: This fixture intentionally contains many similar messages to trigger compression once budgets are tight.
Acknowledged. We'll test compression thresholding at 92% of history budget usage.
